daily_reality.summary: Radiation therapists operate linear accelerators and other equipment to deliver precise radiation treatments to cancer patients. They position patients, verify treatment plans, monitor patients during treatment, and maintain detailed dose records.
typical_tasks: Position patients on treatment table using immobilization devices and imaging
Operate linear accelerators (linacs) to deliver radiation treatments
Verify treatment plans match physician-prescribed doses and targets
Perform image-guided radiation therapy (IGRT) for daily position verification
Monitor patients during treatment for adverse reactions
Maintain detailed radiation dose records for each patient
Perform daily quality assurance checks on treatment machines
Educate patients about treatment process, side effects, and skin care
Calculate and deliver prescribed radiation doses
Communicate with radiation oncologists and medical physicists about treatment plans
Assist with treatment simulation and CT scanning for planning
Provide emotional support to cancer patients throughout treatment course
key_documents: Daily treatment logs and dose records

deadlines.daily_qa: Machine checks before first patient each morning
deadlines.patient_treatments: Schedule of 20-40 patients per day per machine
deadlines.arrt_renewal: Annual certification renewal with biennial CE

daily_reality.seasonality: Relatively steady year-round — cancer treatment doesn't follow seasonal patterns. Some patients delay starting treatment around holidays. Machine maintenance shutdowns may create scheduling pressure.

regulatory.summary: ARRT certification required in most states. Associate's or bachelor's degree from JRCERT-accredited program required. NRC and state radiation regulations govern equipment and safety. Strict quality assurance requirements.

requirements: Associate's or bachelor's degree from JRCERT-accredited program
ARRT Radiation Therapy certification (required in most states)
Annual ARRT renewal with biennial CE (24 credits/2 years)
State licensure required in most states
Some states require additional state examinations
certifying_bodies: ARRT — American Registry of Radiologic Technologists
JRCERT — Joint Review Committee on Education in Radiologic Technology (program accreditation)

regulatory.penalties: Treatment delivery errors can result in facility citations, NRC violations ($100,000+), malpractice lawsuits, and loss of ARRT certification. Patient misadministration requires NRC reporting.

tools.summary: Radiation therapists operate linear accelerators (Varian, Elekta), treatment planning systems (Eclipse, Pinnacle, RayStation), and image guidance systems (CBCT, MR-linac). Equipment costs $2-8 million per linac.

primary_software.name: Treatment Planning Systems (Varian Eclipse, Elekta Monaco, RaySearch RayStation)
primary_software.purpose: Dose calculation and treatment plan optimization

primary_software.name: Record & Verify Systems (Varian ARIA, Elekta MOSAIQ)
primary_software.purpose: Treatment scheduling, documentation, and safety interlocks

primary_software.name: CBCT/IGRT Systems
primary_software.purpose: On-board imaging for daily treatment position verification

primary_software.name: CT Simulator (GE, Siemens, Philips)
primary_software.purpose: Treatment planning CT scans with immobilization

primary_software.name: Brachytherapy afterloaders (Varian, Elekta)
primary_software.purpose: Internal radiation therapy delivery for cervical, prostate, breast cancers

pain_points: Complex treatment plans requiring precise execution
Integration challenges between planning and delivery systems
Cost of equipment maintenance and upgrades ($2-8M per linac)

terminology.summary: Radiation therapists use radiation physics, oncology, and treatment delivery terminology covering dose specification, treatment techniques, and quality assurance.

key_terms.meaning: Linear accelerator — primary external beam radiation treatment machine
Intensity-Modulated Radiation Therapy — advanced dose shaping technique
Volumetric Modulated Arc Therapy — rotational IMRT delivery
Image-Guided Radiation Therapy — imaging before each treatment for positioning
Cone Beam CT — on-board imaging for position verification
Planning Target Volume — treatment target area with margins
Organs At Risk — normal tissues to spare from radiation
Dose-Volume Histogram — graphical treatment plan evaluation
Point in space where radiation beams converge
Tissue-equivalent material placed on skin to modify dose
Patient positioning deviation from planned position
Safety verification procedure before treatment delivery

career_psychology.summary: Radiation therapists earn above-average healthcare salaries ($102K median). Emotionally rewarding but challenging work treating cancer patients daily. High accuracy demands create performance pressure.

career_levels.responsibilities: Treatment delivery under supervision, basic setup and imaging
Independent treatment delivery, all techniques, patient education
Complex cases (SBRT, SRS), student supervision, QA leadership
Department management, staffing, equipment procurement, protocol development

main_fears: Treatment delivery errors (wrong patient, wrong site, wrong dose)
Long-term radiation exposure despite protective measures
burnout_causes: Emotional toll of treating cancer patients daily (some don't survive)
High precision demands with zero tolerance for errors
Repetitive nature of daily treatment sessions
Standing all day and physically positioning patients
Dealing with anxious, fearful, or terminally ill patients
growth_motivation: Specialization in advanced techniques (proton therapy, MR-linac, SBRT)
Medical dosimetry certification (CMD) for treatment planning

market.summary: Median salary $101,990 (BLS May 2024). 2% growth projected 2024-2034 with ~900 annual openings. About 17,600 employed. High salary but slower growth due to treatment technology advances.
market.job_outlook: 2% growth 2024-2034, slower than average. ~900 annual openings from growth and replacements.

work_arrangements.dominant: W-2 employees at hospitals (50%+) and freestanding cancer centers
work_arrangements.travel: Travel radiation therapist positions available at premium

market_trends: Proton therapy center expansion creating specialized positions
MR-linac technology requiring new skill sets
AI-assisted treatment planning and adaptive therapy
Hypofractionation (fewer fractions) reducing per-patient treatment sessions
Flash therapy research potentially changing treatment paradigm
Radiopharmaceutical therapy (theranostics) expanding oncology treatment options
